newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish BPH mulls convertible mark eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Polish BPH mulls convertible mark eurobond.

text.p: The board of Poland's Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA is likely to call an extraordinary shareholders meeting later this year to approve a convertible mark eurobond issue, BPH's president said on Monday.

"The extraordinary shareholders meeting will most likely be called still this year to vote on preparing a convertible bond issue. A large part of it will be placed on the euromarket in German marks," Henryka Pieronkiewicz said.
"BPH's simulation show the cheapest way of raising capital at the moment is through convertible bonds on the euromarket," she told reporters at the bank's headquarters in the southern town of Krakow.
She said BPH also considered offering a part of the bond issue to a Polish bank undergoing privatisation in exchange for between 25 and 30 percent of the other bank's shares.

Pieronkiewicz said the convertible bonds were one of three possible ways of reducing the treasury's 46.6 percent stake in the bank. She said the finance ministry could also offer its shares to a strategic investor, or combine the two options.

Pieronkiewicz said BPH was interested in taking part in the privatisation of Polish banks but declined to give any names. The two banks currently slated for privatisation are Bank Zachodni SA and Powszechny Bank Kredytowy.
Last week Pieronkiewcz said she hoped to find a strategic investor for the treasury's stake in the first quarter of 1997.
BPH, privatised in January 1995, is one of Poland's top 10 banks in terms of capital and assets.

Among BPH's other major shareholders are the Euroepan Bank for Reconstruction and Development with a 15.06 percent stake, and ING Barings and its subsidiary Bank Slaski with a joint 12.6 percent stake.
